issues.description: The three 'wrong' samples are ordinary math errors on problems that base solves 2/2 and that their group mates mostly get right (4/5, 4/5 and 3/5). They are not short-CoT failures: each wrong CoT is near or above its group's length. I checked the golds and all three are right. (a) Sample 10 claims that the convolution of two 6-periodic sequences is 6-periodic. That is false because the sum's range grows with n. The correct answer is 2023, since f = d/dx[1/(1-x+x^2)], which gives coefficient 2023·a_2023 = 2023. (b) Sample 12 computes 15·50/40 = 18.75 instead of 15·40/50 = 12. Then, because the answer must be an integer, it rounds the non-integer to 19 rather than rechecking. The other wrong rollout in its group makes the same error. (c) Sample 11 finds two configurations and picks the wrong one on a 'nice numbers' heuristic. The configuration with ∠BAD = arctan(3/4) gives BC² = 29.29, so the gold 29 is right.
issues.evidence_quote: Sample 10, why='wrong', step 45, qid 48a1010e (gold 2023): 'Thus we can compute c_n for n =0..5. ... Now for n large, we derived periodic for n≥1. So answer 5.'
